facts.statement: Earth's surface acceleration is 9.780 m/s2 at the equator and 9.832 m/s2 at the poles.
Earth's equatorial radius is 6,378.137 km and its polar radius 6,356.752 km; it spins once in 23.9345 hours.
A spring scale calibrated to read 70 kg at a pole reads about 69.6 kg at the equator, about 0.37 kg (370 grams) less, about half a percent.
The equator moves at about 1,674 km/h because of Earth's spin (about 1,670 km/h); the centrifugal effect is 0.034 m/s2, about two thirds of the 0.052 m/s2 difference.
Earth's equator is about 21 km farther from the centre than the poles (6,378 vs 6,357 km); this shape accounts for the remaining third of the difference.

source.method: equatorial minus polar radius; remainder 0.052 - 0.034 m/s2

facts.statement: The Apollo 17 crew photographed the full Earth (the 'Blue Marble') on 7 December 1972.
Earth is slightly squashed: its spin makes it bulge, so the equator is about 21 km farther from the centre than the poles.

source.method: oblate Earth: equatorial radius exceeds polar radius; spinning planets bulge at the equator
